newsitem.title: New Zealand: rugby union - Injuries plague Chiefs as Waratahs loom.
newsitem.headline: rugby union - Injuries plague Chiefs as Waratahs loom.

text.p: HAMILTON, March 5 - A mounting injury toll continues to blight the Waikato Chiefs as they prepare for Saturday night's Super 12 rugby game in Sydney against New South Wales Waratahs.
NZPA reports that Chiefs coach Brad Meurant has made two changes to the team that took the field for an opening-round win against Wellington Hurricanes last Friday.
All Black second five-eighths Walter Little has been ruled out for the Sydney game because of deep bruising to his bottom rib and is replaced by Scott McLeod.
Meurant has also switched his hookers, replacing 22-year-old rookie Greg Smith to give Paul Mitchell matchplay.
Five players named in Saturday night's starting line-up were last night unable to train or only took a limited part in the session because of injury niggles or illness.
Richard Loe has a swollen knee, Ian Foster is still getting over a leg injury, Blair Larsen has an ankle problem, Glen Osborne the flu, and Eric Rush took a knock to his knee during training.
"None of our injuries, apart from Deon Muir, are ultra-serious. It's just wear and tear on bodies, the games are that physically intense," Chiefs manager Steve Gilbert said.

With No 8 Muir expected to be out for several weeks with his ankle injury and blind-side flanker Richard Coventry still recovering from a groin strain, the Chiefs are severely short of back-up at lock and tight/loose forwards in the build-up to the match against the Waratahs.

Chiefs: Matthew Cooper, Glen Osborne, Frank Bunce, Eric Rush, Scott McLeod, Ian Foster, Mark Robinson, Errol Brain, Dean Anglesey, Glenn Taylor, Ian Jones (capt), Blair Larsen, Richard Loe, Paul Mitchell, Michael Collins. Reserves: backs, Bruce Reihana, Nicky Little, Rhys Duggan; forwards, Brett Sinkinson, Lee Lidgard, Greg Smith.
